newsitem.title: USA: Blast in Atlanta raises fears of serial bomber.
newsitem.headline: Blast in Atlanta raises fears of serial bomber.

text.p: A bomb that exploded on Friday night at a popular gay and lesbian nightclub injured at least five people, raising fears that a serial bomber could be at work in Atlanta, the FBI said on Saturday.

The fourth bomb to strike the city in seven months exploded in the rear patio section of the Otherside Lounge of Atlanta shortly before 10 p.m. EST (0300 GMT on Saturday). Staff said there were between 40 and 50 people inside the nightclub at the time.

Members of the Atlanta SWAT team, believing that a shooting had occurred, arrived on the scene and soon spotted a suspicious-looking backpack outside the nightclub in a nearby parking lot. The city bomb squad discovered a second device inside the bag and, after midnight, used a robot to carry out a controlled detonation.

Investigators from the FBI and the U.S. Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco and Firearms said the attack bore similarities to both a January double-bombing at an Atlanta abortion clinic and the deadly July attack on the Atlanta Summer Games known as the Centennial Olympic Park bombing.
"We all recognise that there are similarities here. We will be searching out the possibility that we have a serial bomber," FBI special agent Woody Johnson told a news conference early on Saturday.
Of the five people injured in the nightclub explosion, only one woman required hospitalization. She was later reported in stable condition.

Nightclub patrons reported seeing a flash followed by a blast which they said resembled an exploding electrical transformer. Several local news reports said the bomb was apparently packed with nails and quoted eyewitnesses as saying that some of the victims had nails sticking out of their arms.
Federal officials sought leads from members of the public through the special ATF hotline, 1-888-ATF-BOMB, as members of the ATF's National Reponse Team headed to Atlanta from Washington.
"We clearly believe that we are dealing with a deranged killer, but one that is very clever as well," Atlanta Mayor Bill Campbell said.
Police investigators said Friday's bombing resembled a double-bomb attack on an Atlanta abortion clinic in January that injured half a dozen people, mostly law enforcement agents and rescue workers.
As in that attack, the second device at the nightclub was placed in an apparent attempt to injure police and rescue workers responding to the initial emergency call.
Both the clinic and the nightclub bombings also came without warning.

The use of a backpack for the second device resembled the Centennial Olympic Park bombing in July. In that incident, a pipe bomb contained in a green military-style knapsack exploded during a crowded outdoor concert in downtown Atlanta, leaving two people dead and more than 100 wounded.
Both the abortion-clinic bombing and the Centennial Olympic Park bombing remain unsolved.
